{
  "frontend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implement UI and client changes to support the new sort behavior and default, without changing search (q), count, or pagination semantics.

Required changes:
1) New sort option
   - Add a new sort value "title_desc" to the existing sort selector/options.
   - The option value MUST be exactly "title_desc" so it matches the backend contract.
   - Keep the existing "created_at_desc" option present and working (do not remove or deprecate it).

2) Default sort
   - Change the client-side default sort selection to "title_asc". Where the UI or client initializes list requests with a default sort, set that default to "title_asc".
   - If your code sometimes omits the sort query parameter and relies on the server default, update the UI to explicitly include sort=title_asc in requests when no user selection exists OR coordinate with backend so both sides use title_asc as the default. (Both frontend and backend will be updated; prefer explicitly sending sort=title_asc from the client to make behavior deterministic.)

3) Request generation and preservation of other params
   - When user selects a sort option, include the query parameter sort=<value> (e.g., sort=title_desc or sort=title_asc) in list requests.
   - Preserve all other query parameters (q, count, pagination tokens/page numbers/offset) when adding/changing the sort parameter. Do not drop or rewrite q, count, or pagination parameters.
   - When changing sort, ensure pagination semantics remain consistent (for example, reset page or cursor as appropriate per existing UX rules). Do not change how pagination behaves other than necessary resets already in product behavior.

4) UI labeling and state
   - Use the same labeling and ordering conventions used by other sort options (do not invent new UI patterns). Ensure the default selection displayed in the UI reflects title_asc.
   - If the client persists sort selection (localStorage, user settings, URL), persist the new default/selection consistently.

5) Tests and QA
   - Add/adjust unit tests for the sort selector and API client to verify that selecting the new option sends sort=title_desc and that default requests send sort=title_asc when appropriate.
   - Add/adjust integration/e2e tests to verify: a) lists with identical titles are ordered as the backend guarantees (the frontend must not assume further tie-breaking), b) created_at_desc option still functions, c) q, count, and pagination behavior is unchanged when sort is changed.

6) Documentation/Client SDK
   - Update any client-side API docs, examples, or SDK code to list the new sort value "title_desc" and to show default as "title_asc".

Notes/constraints (do not assume or change):
- Do not attempt to implement or reproduce server-side tie-breaking logic in the frontend; trust the backend to order by UUID as the secondary key. The frontend should only set sort=<value> and preserve pagination state as currently defined.
- Do not change query parameter names or pagination semantics. If there are unresolved questions about where default is enforced (client vs server), coordinate with backend but ensure the client explicitly sends sort=title_asc where feasible."
  },
  "backend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implement server-side support for the new sort value and change the API default to title_asc, while preserving existing search, count, and pagination semantics.

Required changes:
1) New sort value
   - Accept a new sort parameter value "title_desc".
   - Map sort=title_desc to ordering: primary key title DESC, secondary key uuid ASC. Example SQL semantics: ORDER BY title DESC, uuid ASC.

2) Default sort change
   - When no explicit sort parameter is provided by the request, use title_asc as the API default.
   - Map title_asc to ordering: primary key title ASC, secondary key uuid ASC. Example SQL: ORDER BY title ASC, uuid ASC.
   - Note: frontend will be updated to often send sort=title_asc explicitly; still implement server-side default to ensure consistency for clients that omit the parameter.

3) Preserve created_at_desc and backward compatibility
   - Keep existing support for sort=created_at_desc unchanged. Do not treat it as deprecated or reject requests using it.
   - Ensure any other existing sort values remain supported as before.

4) Pagination semantics
   - Maintain current pagination semantics (do not change meaning of q, count, page/cursor/offset).
   - If pagination is offset-based: ensure ORDER BY includes the secondary key uuid for both title_asc and title_desc so that tie-breaking is stable (ORDER BY title ASC/DESC, uuid ASC). This prevents inconsistent ordering across pages when titles duplicate.
   - If pagination is cursor-based: include both title and uuid in the cursor key for title_asc and title_desc cases. For title_desc, comparison logic must reflect title descending then uuid ascending when constructing/consuming cursors/tokens.
   - Ensure changing sort does not alter the semantics of q, count, or pagination beyond the natural effect of a different ordering.

5) Query/filtering
   - Keep existing q (search) filtering and count semantics unchanged. Apply sorting after existing filtering and before pagination as the current pipeline does.

6) Tests and QA
   - Add unit tests for query builder / ORM mapping to confirm that: a) sort=title_desc produces ORDER BY title DESC, uuid ASC; b) title_asc produces ORDER BY title ASC, uuid ASC; c) existing created_at_desc behavior is unchanged.
   - Add integration tests that verify stable ordering across pages when multiple items share the same title (tie-break by uuid ASC) and that cursors/continuation tokens are generated and consumed correctly when title ordering is used.
   - Add acceptance tests verifying default behavior when sort param is absent (title_asc), and that requests with sort=created_at_desc still function.

7) Documentation and API contract
   - Update API documentation to list the new sort value "title_desc" and to indicate that the default when omitted is "title_asc".
   - Communicate the change of default sort to API consumers (changelog or release note), since default used to differ.

Notes/constraints (do not assume or change):
- Preserve existing collation, null-handling, and case-sensitivity behavior for title ordering—do not change how title values are compared beyond direction (ASC/DESC) and the guaranteed secondary uuid ASC tie-breaker.
- Do not change the names of query parameters (e.g., do not rename sort/q/count/page). If there are unresolved questions about pagination implementation details (cursor format, token encoding), modify cursor logic only to include title+uuid where necessary and coordinate with frontend to ensure tokens remain compatible."
  }
}
